title: The Static of the Kuiper Line Revisited
premise: Felix Pemberton, a starship navigator who faked their own death seven years ago to escape a war-crimes tribunal, discovers a manifest anomaly: a name — their real one — listed on a ship that officially never flew. Chasing the phantom manifest leads Felix to the Kuiper Line, a derelict relay where the original Felix's backup consciousness has been sleeping, holding a decryption key that can either expose the atrocity Felix fled or frame the fleet admiral who ordered it. Hunted by a tribunal agent who is also their former co-pilot, Felix must choose between destroying the backup and preserving their invented identity, or waking it and surrendering themselves to a justice that may be a lie. In the end, Felix broadcasts the admiral's guilt, lets the backup wake in their old body, and accepts exile — invisible again, but finally honest about why.
about_author: Wendell Oyelaran is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that would never meet, a career he describes as 'narrating other people's arrivals.' He writes near-future fiction about people who survive by becoming someone else, and lives off-grid with a shortwave rig he refuses to explain.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Routine cargo run through contested orbits; a customs scan flags a name on a manifest for the Meridian Vale, a ship destroyed seven years ago. The name is Pemberton — Felix's original name. Emotional beat: the cold dread of a past self surfacing after years of careful erasure.

chapters.title: The Person You Were Is Cargo
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix investigates the flag and finds the manifest originated from the Kuiper Line relay, decommissioned but still drawing power. Their co-pilot Dara notices Felix's shaking hands. Beat: paranoia tightening; Felix lies to the one person they trust.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Felix's POV. The Meridian Vale's final voyage: an order to burn a refugee flotilla, Felix's refusal, the tribunal summons, and the desperate identity swap that left 'Felix Pemberton' officially dead. Beat: guilt revealed as the engine of Felix's invisibility.

chapters.title: A Visit from the Registry
chapters.summary: Tribunal agent Ilsa Voss's POV. Voss, once Felix's co-pilot, arrives at the station under a customs pretext, carrying a warrant sealed seven years ago. She suspects the manifest is bait — someone wants Felix found. Beat: her divided loyalty between duty and old affection.

chapters.title: Dead Drop at the Kuiper Line
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix slips away to the relay and finds a live terminal addressed to them, containing a partial decryption key and a message: 'Wake me or the war starts without you.' Beat: the trap becomes an invitation; Felix realizes the backup is the sender.

chapters.title: The Hold Full of Sleepers
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix confronts the ship's own backup bay — copies of their original mind, legally contraband, bought as insurance. One copy is missing: the one at Kuiper Line. Beat: horror at the self they sold to survive.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Warrant
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss decodes the manifest trail and confirms the navigator she's hunting is the person she flew beside for three years. She requests a pursuit vessel and is denied — someone above her is blocking it. Beat: suspicion that the tribunal itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Dara Asks the Wrong Question
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Dara confronts Felix about the Meridian Vale, having pulled the flight records herself. Felix gives her a half-truth. Beat: the cost of survival made intimate — Dara chooses to stay, and that choice becomes a debt.

chapters.title: The Admiral's Silence
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss traces the manifest's origin to the office of Admiral Corven Hask, the man who ordered the flotilla burned. The manifest was planted to flush out the backup before it can testify. Beat: the hunter realizes her prey may be the only witness left.

chapters.title: Running the Contested Orbits
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A chase sequence: Hask's private contractors corner Felix's ship in a debris field. Felix uses navigator's tricks — gravity slingshots, dead transponder runs — to escape. Beat: survival instinct as competence and as curse; a contractor dies because of Felix's flying.

chapters.title: What the Backup Remembers
chapters.summary: The backup's POV, in second person — a consciousness dreaming in storage. It remembers the flotilla, the order, and the moment original Felix agreed to testify before fleeing. It has spent seven years composing a message. Beat: sympathy for the self Felix abandoned.

chapters.title: Negotiation with Yourself
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix reaches the Kuiper Line again and opens a channel to the backup. It offers a deal: wake it, and it testifies; refuse, and it broadcasts the raw flight logs — implicating Felix's flight as much as Hask's order. Beat: the war inside the self made literal.

chapters.title: Voss Boards the Vale's Wreck
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss searches the Meridian Vale's drifting wreck and finds the black box Hask's people missed — proof the burn order was given twice, and Felix refused it twice. Beat: Voss's warrant starts to feel like an instrument of the crime it punishes.

chapters.title: The Price of the Key
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The backup reveals the full decryption key requires a live neural handshake — waking it means Felix's current identity legally dies, since two Pembertons cannot exist. Felix hesitates. Beat: the theme crystallized — identity as the final currency.

chapters.title: Dara's Choice
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Hask's contractors capture Dara to draw Felix out. Offered her ship and record in exchange for Felix's location, Dara gives them a false heading and takes a beating for it. Beat: loyalty repaid at cost; Felix learns what their lie has cost others.

chapters.title: The Exchange at Perihelion
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix trades themselves to the contractors for Dara, expecting a cell, and is instead delivered to Admiral Hask, who offers Felix full amnesty to testify that the flotilla burned itself. Beat: the seduction of survival — the same bargain, seven years later, at a higher price.

chapters.title: The Man Who Gave the Order
chapters.summary: Hask's POV. Hask rationalizes the burn as arithmetic — three hundred crew against forty thousand refugees — and sees Felix's refusal as sentimental malfunction. He genuinely believes he is offering mercy. Beat: the antagonist made comprehensible, which makes him worse.

chapters.title: Wake Me
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In Hask's custody, Felix transmits the wake command from a holding cell terminal. Across the system, at the Kuiper Line, the backup opens its eyes in a borrowed body. Beat: the point of no return, rendered quiet and enormous.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Backup's POV. The awakened Felix, in the original body, seizes the relay's transmitter and broadcasts the black box, the decryption key, and the flight logs — Hask's order, Felix's refusals, all of it, unedited, to every contested orbit at once. Beat: catharsis; truth as a weapon that wounds everyone holding it.

chapters.title: Tribunal, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss arrests Hask on the strength of the broadcast, then turns to the two Pembertons and must decide what justice means when the fugitive is also the key witness. She voids the seven-year warrant and issues a new one for Hask. Beat: justice achieved outside the law that failed to deliver it.

chapters.title: Two of Everything
chapters.summary: Felix and the backup, alternating. The two versions of Felix meet aboard the relay: one who ran, one who waited. They divide the name, the debts, the memories. Beat: reconciliation without resolution — you cannot merge back into who you were.

chapters.title: The Static of the Kuiper Line
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, epilogue. The original Felix takes a new name and a navigator's post on a relief convoy; the backup keeps the relay, tending the signal. Dara visits once. Felix finally sleeps without checking the hold. Beat: the price of survival paid in full — invisibility chosen, at last, honestly.
